newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore libel case defence lawyers seek opt out.
newsitem.headline: Singapore libel case defence lawyers seek opt out.

text.p: Lawyers acting for a Singapore opposition politician in 13 defamation lawsuits filed by members of the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) have asked the High Court to allow them to pull out, the Straits Times reported.

Peter Low and Loo Ngan Chor felt it would be impossible to remain as the lawyers of Tang Liang Hong after statements he made about them in an interview with the Straits Times on Tuesday, the daily said on Thursday.
The lawyers could not be reached for comment due to a holiday in Singapore.

The newspaper said their application would be heard by the court on Friday, before the start of a hearing on May 5 to determine the costs Tang must pay for the lawsuits he lost involving Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and 10 other PAP leaders.
Tang had told the newspaper that he was disappointed by his lawyers' failure to file his 60-page affidavit rebutting allegations made against him by PAP leaders.
"They think some of my affidavit contains allegations which they are scared may jeopardise their position as my solicitors," it quoted Tang as saying.
Tang did not specify what these allegations were or how the lawyers' positions might be jeopardised.
Tang was an unsuccessful candidate for the Worker's Party in Singapore's January 2 general election and fled the city state shortly afterwards saying he feared for his life.

His previous lawyer, Joshua Jeyaretnam, was recently referred to the Law Society's disciplinary committee after a judge ruled he had failed to ensure there was enough evidence to support Tang's bid to stop the judge hearing the 13 suits.
None of the lawyers involved in that hearing would explain why Tang thought the judge should stand aside.
